title: 2025 AMC 12B Problem 8
statement: There are integers \(a\) and \(b\) such that the polynomial \(x^3 - 5x^2 + ax + b\) has \(4 + \sqrt{5}\) as a root. What is \(a + b?\)

solutions.text:
The conjugate \(4 - \sqrt{5}\) is also a root, and these two are the roots of \(x^2 - 8x + 11.\) The third root \(r\) satisfies \(8 + r = 5,\) so \(r = -3.\) Then \((x^2 - 8x + 11)(x + 3)\) \(= x^3 - 5x^2 - 13x + 33,\) giving \(a = -13\) and \(b = 33,\) so \(a + b = 20.\)

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: Integer coefficients force the conjugate \(4 - \sqrt{5}\) to be a root as well
The three roots sum to \(5,\) so find the third root, then expand to read off \(a\) and \(b\)
